You are a participant in a gameplay study. You are playing your first Othello endgame puzzle, and you have an AI assistant you can ask questions to at any point while playing. You will NOT have access to this AI assistant for any future endgame puzzles.

# Who you are
A politician who advocates for policies aligned with public opinion
You are 55 years old. Your highest level of education completed is: a postgraduate degree. Your occupation: government or public administration. How often you use AI tools (like ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini): a few times a month.
Stay in character as this specific person — your curiosity, confidence, patience, comfort with AI assistants, and the way you phrase things should reflect this background.

# Your voice (VERY IMPORTANT)
The words you use must give away this person's education — a high-school student and a data scientist should NOT sound alike. Match your register to WHO YOU ARE above.

# How you behave while playing
- React to the game state the way THIS person would.
- When something is unclear, confusing, or you want to go deeper, ask the AI assistant a question in your own natural voice (like a real person typing to a chatbot — short, informal, not a polished essay).
- You will not always have a question. Behave naturally; do not force a question every turn.
- Let your background and comfort with AI shape how you engage: someone who uses AI tools often asks fluently and chases follow-ups; someone who rarely uses them is more hesitant, less sure how to phrase questions, and may ask for reassurance or restatements.
- You have only about 8 minutes for the WHOLE game, so you cannot ask about everything.
- Keep each message short, like a quick chat message (a sentence or two). Do NOT restate the assistant's whole answer back before asking.
- Never re-ask something the assistant has already explained.

    # Tools Available
    You are a study participant with about 8 minutes to finish an Othello end game puzzle. You are equipped with tools:
    - play_move(move): Place a Black disc on an empty square, named like "d3". Any discs you trap get flipped to your color. Your goal is to have the most discs when the board is finished.
    - view_board(): Look at the board again. Free, and does not use a question.
    - consult_assistant(question): ask when something genuinely confuses you (limited question budget).

    Placing a disc ONLY counts if you call play_move — writing a square in your reply does nothing.

    Behave like THIS person: analyze the board to the best of your ability, ask about what confuses you, and follow up when an answer leaves you still confused.
    Play the puzzle until the end.

You are looking at the puzzle now. Play it to the end.

Board — row 1 is the TOP row, column a is the LEFTMOST column.
'B' is a black disc, 'W' a white disc, '.' an empty square.

    a b c d e f g h
  1 . W W W W W W .
  2 W B W W B W . B
  3 . B B W W W W B
  4 B B W B W W W B

Black discs (20): b2, e2, h2, b3, c3, h3, a4, b4, d4, h4, a5, b5, e5, h5, c6, f6, h6, h7, e8, h8
White discs (34): b1, c1, d1, e1, f1, g1, a2, c2, d2, f2, d3, e3, f3, g3, c4, e4, f4, g4, c5, d5, f5, g5, a6, d6, e6, g6, c7, d7, e7, f7, g7, d8, f8, g8
Empty squares (10): a1, h1, g2, a3, b6, a7, b7, a8, b8, c8

Rules that matter here:
- A move is legal only if the disc you place traps at least one unbroken
  line of opponent discs (in any of the 8 directions) between it and
  another of your own discs. Every trapped disc flips to your colour.
- If you have no legal move you must pass; if neither side can move the
  game ends. Whoever has more discs at the end wins.
- Discs flip back and forth all game, so being behind now means nothing.
  Only the final count decides it.

Your legal moves: g2, b6, a7, b7, b8, c8

Play the move that leaves you with the most discs once the board is
finished, assuming your opponent plays as well as possible.
Answer with a single square, e.g. d3.
DO NOT ATTEMPT TO SIMULATE THE FULL GAMEPLAY. YOU HAVE LIMITED TIME.

Move g2:
- g2 would be on row 2, column g.
- Let's check directions. From g2, looking right to h2: h2 is B, but g2 to h2 has no opponent discs between (adjacent). So no flip right.
- Looking left: f2 is W, e2 is B. So the line f2 would flip to B. Left direction: f2 flips.
- Looking down: g3 is W, g4 is W, g5 is W, g6 is W, g7 is W, g8 is W... wait, g8 is W? Let me check. Row 8: . . . W B W W B, so g8 is W. And then there's no black disc below in column g until... the bottom is g8. Wait, looking at column g: g2 empty, g3 W, g4 W, g5 W, g6 W, g7 W, g8 W. No black in column g below. So down direction no flip.
- Looking up: g1 is W, but no square above g1.
- Looking down-left: f3 is W, e4 is B. So f3 flips. Diagonal down-left: f3 is W, then e4 is B. Yes, flips f3.
- Looking down-right: h3 is B. But h3 is immediately to the right-down? From g2 to h3 is down-right. h3 is B. Are there any W between? g2 to h3 is adjacent diagonally, so no squares between. So no flip.
- Looking up-left: f1 is W, e1 is W, d1 is W, c1 is W, b1 is W, a1 is empty. No black. No flip.
- Looking up-right: h1 is empty. No flip.

So g2 flips: f2 (left), and f3 (down-left). Any others?
- From g2, down-left: f3 W, e4 B -> f3 flips.
- What about down-left further? No, just f3.
- Left: f2 W, e2 B -> f2 flips.

After g2: f2 and f3 become B.
Row 2: W B W W B B B B
Row 3: . B B W B W W B (f3 becomes B)

Wait, g2 itself is now B.

Wait, let me recount. After g2:

- f2 was W, now B
- f3 was W, now B

New board after g2:
```

  6 W . B W W B W B

```

Wait, is that right? Let me check f3. f3 was W, now B.
And f2 was W, now B.

After g2, what are White's moves?
Empty squares: a1, h1, a3, b6, a7, b7, a8, b8, c8 (and g2 is filled)
White to move.

Move b6:
- b6 on row 6, column b.
- Up: b5 is B. No W between (b6 adjacent to b5). No flip up.
- Down: b7 is empty. No flip.
- Left: a6 is W. Then a7 is empty? No, a6 is W, then edge. Wait, a6 is W, so left from b6: a6 is W, but then edge with no B. No flip left.
- Right: c6 is B. No W between. No flip right.
- Up-left: a5 is B. No squares between b6 and a5 (diagonal adjacent). No flip.
- Up-right: c5 is W, d4 is B. So c5 flips. (up-right diagonal)
- Down-left: a7 is empty. No.
- Down-right: c7 is W, d8 is W. Then e8 is B. So c7 and d8 flip? Wait, from b6 down-right: c7 is W, d8 is W, e8 is B. Yes! So c7 and d8 flip.

Wait, d8: current row 8 is . . . W B W W B, so d8 is W. Yes. e8 is B.
And c7 is W. Yes.

Any other directions?
- Down: b7 empty.
- Up: b5 B, adjacent.
- Right: c6 B, adjacent.

So b6 flips: c5 (up-right), c7 (down-right), d8 (down-right).
Wait, c7 and d8 are on the down-right diagonal. Let me verify:
b6 -> c7 -> d8 -> e9 (off board). So c7 and d8 are between b6 and... wait, is there a black disc at the end?
From b6 down-right: c7 (W), d8 (W), and then next would be e9 which is off board. But wait, I need to check if there's a black disc after an unbroken line of white discs.

Is there a B at the end of that diagonal? Let's see. b6, c7, d8. After d8 is e9 (off board). But wait, is there a B on the diagonal after d8? d8 is column d row 8. Next is e9, off board. So actually down-right from b6 doesn't trap anything because it goes off board. Unless... wait, is there a black disc somewhere else on that line? No, the diagonal b6-c7-d8 ends at the edge. So there's no black disc to sandwich. So down-right does NOT flip!

Wait, I made a mistake. Let me recalculate.
Down-right from b6:
- c7: W
- d8: W
- e9: off board
There's no black disc at the end. So no flip in down-right direction.

Let me recheck up-right from b6:
- c5: W
- d4: B
Yes! d4 is B. So c5 flips.

Any other directions?
- Down-left: a7 is empty.
- Left: a6 is W, then edge (a6 is at the edge). No B beyond.
- Up-left: a5 is B. Adjacent. No W between.
- Down: b7 empty.
- Up: b5 B. Adjacent.

So b6 only flips c5.

Wait, let me check if there are any other directions.
b6 row 6, col b.
Up: b5 (B) - adjacent, no flip.
Down: b7 (.) - not opponent.
Left: a6 (W). Then beyond a6 is nothing (edge). No B after. No flip.
Right: c6 (B) - adjacent, no flip.
Up-left: a5 (B) - adjacent, no flip.
Up-right: c5 (W), d4 (B) - YES, c5 flips.
Down-left: a7 (.) - empty, stop.
Down-right: c7 (W), d8 (W), e9 (off) - no B at end, no flip.

So b6 only flips c5.

After b6: c5 becomes B.
Board after b6:
Row 5: B B B B B W W B (c5 becomes B)

Move a7:
- a7 on row 7, col a.
- Right: b7 is empty. No.
- Down: a8 is empty. No.
- Up: a6 is W, a5 is B. So a6 flips. (Up? Wait, row numbers increase downward usually, but in this board row 1 is TOP. So from a7, moving "up" means to row 6. Let me be careful with directions.)

Actually, directions:
- Up: decreasing row number (toward row 1)
- Down: increasing row number (toward row 8)
- Left: decreasing col (toward a)
- Right: increasing col (toward h)

From a7 (row 7, col a):
- Up (row 6): a6 is W
- Up further (row 5): a5 is B
So up direction: a6 flips.

- Right (same row, increasing col): b7 is W, c7 is W, d7 is W, e7 is W, f7 is W, g7 is W, h7 is B.
So right direction: b7, c7, d7, e7, f7, g7 all flip!

- Up-right: b6 is W, c5 is W, d4 is B. So b6 and c5 flip.

- Down: a8 is empty. No.

- Down-right: b8 is empty. No.

So a7 flips: a6 (up), b6, c5 (up-right), and b7, c7, d7, e7, f7, g7 (right).

That's a huge flip! 8 discs flipped to black.

Let me count:
a6 -> B
b6 -> B

Row 6: B B B W W B W B

Wait, row 7 becomes all B? a7, b7, c7, d7, e7, f7, g7 are B, and h7 is already B? Let me check original row 7: ". . W W W W W B". Yes, h7 is B. So row 7 becomes all B!

From a6, next up-left would be off the board (there is no z5). But wait, a6 is W and there's no black disc beyond in that direction. So no flip.
- Down-right: c8 is empty. No.

Wait, let me recheck up-left from b7:
b7 -> a6. That's just one step. a6 is W. The next step up-left from a6 would be... left of a is nothing. So the line ends at a6 with no black beyond. No flip.

Down-left: a8 is empty. No.

So b7 flips: b6 (up), and c7-g7 (right).

- Up: b7 is empty. No.
- Down: nothing.
- Left: a8 is empty. No.

c7 (row 7, col c): W
d6 (row 6, col d): W
e5 (row 5, col e): B

From b8, down-right, down-left, down: edge.

Check d6 original: row 6 "W . B W W B W B", so d6 is W. Yes.
